https://www.barrons.com/articles/jabil-apple-contractor-rises-on-fyq2-beat-ceo-sees-broad-based-growth-1521147654 Jabil, Apple Contractor, Rises on FYQ2 Beat, CEO Sees ‘Broad-based Growth’ By March 15, 2018 5:00 p.m. ET Text Size Medium Large 
Jabil ( JBL ), the contract manufacturer that is an important contractor to Apple ( AAPL ), among others, is seeing its shares rise 71 cents, or 2.5%, in late trading, at $29.20, after the company this afternoon reported fiscal Q2 revenue and profit that topped analysts’ expectations, and forecast this quarter’s revenue higher as well. 
CEO Mark Mondello said the company was “pleased” with the results, including “strong” revenue growth, and “healthy cash flow generation." 
Mondello said actions such as a renewal of the company’s 10-year senior notes at more-favorable rates "position us well as we remain focused on diversifying our earnings and cash flows." 
Revenue in the three months ended in February rose 19%, year over year, to $5.3 billion, yielding EPS of 66 cents, excluding some costs. 
Analysts had been modeling $4.9 billion and 62 cents per share. 
For the current quarter , the company sees revenue of $4.75 billion to $5.05 billion, and EPS of 35 cents to 55 cents. That compares to consensus for $4.82 billion and 45 cents per share. 
Mondello reiterated a goal of $2.60 per share in earnings this fiscal year, saying the company expects that the second half of the fiscal year will bring "broad-based growth across both of our segments,” referring to Jabil’s “Diversified Manufacturing Services,” or DMS, business unit, and to its "Electronics Manufacturing Services,” or EMS, business. 
Mondello added, "we remain committed to delivering $1 billion in operating cash flows” this fiscal year. Most Popular
